### What It Does & How It Works
AresHUD (Martian Map) is a hands-free Augmented Reality (AR) astronaut helmet heads-up display and survival navigation system for Mars. Designed for high-contrast visibility in harsh Martian lighting, it projects real-time planetary data directly onto the astronaut's visor:
1. Subsurface Water-Ice Detection: Highlights high-probability underground water-ice deposits (up to 92.5% confidence) inside craters to guide life-support and resource extraction.
2. Real-Time Radiation Hazard Alerts: Triggers immediate visual warnings and recalculates safe navigation routes when solar radiation spikes.
3. Thermal Terrain Mapping: Displays live surface temperature distributions (-125°C to 20°C) so crews can avoid extreme cold zones.
4. Landmark & Mission Telemetry: Tracks major geological landmarks (such as Olympus Mons), oxygen levels, mission progress, and safe base waypoints.

### Tools, Software & Development Factors
We used Canva Pro to design the high-contrast HUD interfaces and assemble the demonstration presentation, integrating authentic NASA planetary datasets for accurate environmental parameters. During development, we prioritized astronaut cognitive load reduction, emergency response speed, and clear visual hierarchy under extreme spacesuit visibility constraints.

### Intended Impact & AI Disclosure
By transforming complex NASA planetary data into intuitive, real-time visual guidance, AresHUD accelerates emergency decision-making and enhances astronaut safety on future Mars missions. (Note: AI tools were utilized in Canva for background visual animations and text-to-speech voiceover narration in the demonstration video.)
